slot.topic_title: Introducing Calculus: Can Change Occur at an Instant?

item.title: Average Velocities Approaching an Instantaneous Velocity
item.stimulus: A ball is thrown straight up. Its height above the ground, in meters, t seconds after it is thrown is s(t) = 40t − 5t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 8. The questions below focus on the instant t = 2 seconds.
item.model_answer:
(a) s(2) = 80 − 20 = 60, s(2.1) = 84 − 22.05 = 61.95, s(1.9) = 76 − 18.05 = 57.95.
Over [2, 2.1]: (61.95 − 60)/(2.1 − 2) = 1.95/0.1 = 19.5 meters per second.
Over [1.9, 2]: (60 − 57.95)/(2 − 1.9) = 2.05/0.1 = 20.5 meters per second.

(b) s(2 + h) = 40(2 + h) − 5(4 + 4h + h²) = 80 + 40h − 20 − 20h − 5h² = 60 + 20h − 5h².
s(2 + h) − s(2) = 60 + 20h − 5h² − 60 = 20h − 5h².
For h ≠ 0: [s(2 + h) − s(2)]/h = (20h − 5h²)/h = 20 − 5h.
At h = 0 the interval has zero length, so the change in time is 0. The quotient would be 0/0, which requires dividing by zero, so the average velocity is undefined at h = 0.

(c) The instantaneous velocity at t = 2 is the limit of the average velocities as the interval shrinks:
lim h→0 [s(2 + h) − s(2)]/h = lim h→0 (20 − 5h) = 20 meters per second.
The part (a) values correspond to h = 0.1 (20 − 0.5 = 19.5) and h = −0.1 (20 + 0.5 = 20.5). The value 20 lies between 19.5 and 20.5, and as h gets closer to 0 on either side, 20 − 5h gets closer to 20, so the average velocities over shrinking intervals containing t = 2 approach 20 m/s.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction as F
import sympy as sp
s=lambda t: 40*t-5*t**2
assert s(F(2))==60
assert s(F(21,10))==F(6195,100)
assert s(F(19,10))==F(5795,100)
a1=(s(F(21,10))-s(F(2)))/F(1,10)
a2=(s(F(2))-s(F(19,10)))/F(1,10)
assert a1==F(39,2)
assert a2==F(41,2)
h=sp.symbols('h')
S=lambda t: 40*t-5*t**2
assert sp.expand(S(2+h))==sp.expand(60+20*h-5*h**2)
assert sp.expand(S(2+h)-S(2))==sp.expand(20*h-5*h**2)
q=sp.simplify((S(2+h)-S(2))/h)
assert sp.simplify(q-(20-5*h))==0
L=sp.limit((S(2+h)-S(2))/h,h,0)
assert L==20
assert (20-5*F(1,10))==a1 and (20-5*F(-1,10))==a2
assert a1<20<a2
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

parts.prompt: Find the average velocity of the ball over the time interval [2, 2.1] and over the time interval [1.9, 2]. Show the computations and include units.

criteria.text: Average velocity over [2, 2.1] is 19.5 meters per second.
criteria.evidence: Shows s(2.1) − s(2) divided by 0.1, for example (61.95 − 60)/0.1, giving 19.5 m/s.
criteria.fix: Compute s at both endpoints, subtract, then divide by the length of the time interval, 0.1 seconds.

criteria.text: Average velocity over [1.9, 2] is 20.5 meters per second.
criteria.evidence: Shows s(2) − s(1.9) divided by 0.1, for example (60 − 57.95)/0.1, giving 20.5 m/s.
criteria.fix: Evaluate s(1.9) = 76 − 18.05 carefully, then divide the change in height by the change in time.

parts.prompt: For h ≠ 0, the average velocity of the ball over the time interval with endpoints 2 and 2 + h is [s(2 + h) − s(2)]/h. Show that this expression simplifies to 20 − 5h. Then explain why the expression [s(2 + h) − s(2)]/h cannot be evaluated at h = 0.

criteria.text: Finds the change in height s(2 + h) − s(2) = 20h − 5h².
criteria.evidence: Expands s(2 + h) = 40(2 + h) − 5(2 + h)² = 60 + 20h − 5h² and subtracts s(2) = 60 to get 20h − 5h².
criteria.fix: Expand (2 + h)² as 4 + 4h + h² before multiplying by −5, then subtract s(2) = 60.

criteria.text: Divides by h (h ≠ 0) to obtain the average velocity 20 − 5h.
criteria.evidence: Shows (20h − 5h²)/h = 20 − 5h, noting the division is valid because h ≠ 0.
criteria.fix: Factor h out of the numerator and cancel it, stating that cancellation is allowed only because h ≠ 0.

criteria.text: Explains that at h = 0 the change in time is zero, so the quotient would require division by zero (0/0) and the average velocity is undefined.
criteria.evidence: States that h = 0 means the interval has zero length, the denominator is 0 (the expression becomes 0/0), so an average rate of change cannot be computed there.
criteria.fix: Point out that an average rate divides by the change in the independent variable, and that change is zero when h = 0.

parts.prompt: Use the result of part (b) to find the instantaneous velocity of the ball at t = 2 as a limit of average velocities, with units. Then explain how your two answers from part (a) are consistent with this value.

criteria.text: Instantaneous velocity at t = 2 is lim h→0 (20 − 5h) = 20 meters per second.
criteria.evidence: Writes the limit of the average velocity as h→0 (not substituting h = 0 into the original quotient) and obtains 20 m/s with units.
criteria.fix: Write lim h→0 of the simplified average velocity 20 − 5h, then evaluate; include meters per second.

criteria.text: Explains consistency: 20 lies between 19.5 and 20.5, the average velocities on short intervals on each side of t = 2, and averages approach 20 as the intervals shrink.
criteria.evidence: Notes that 19.5 < 20 < 20.5 and that these come from h = 0.1 and h = −0.1 in 20 − 5h, so shrinking the interval moves the averages toward 20.
criteria.fix: Compare the part (a) averages with the limit value and note they come from intervals of length 0.1 on either side of t = 2.

item.title: Average Velocities Approaching an Instant for a Thrown Ball
item.stimulus: A ball is thrown upward. Its height above the ground, in feet, t seconds after it is thrown is s(t) = 64t − 16t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. For a nonzero number h, consider the time interval between t = 1 and t = 1 + h.
item.model_answer:
(a) s(1) = 64 − 16 = 48. s(1 + h) = 64(1 + h) − 16(1 + 2h + h²) = 64 + 64h − 16 − 32h − 16h² = 48 + 32h − 16h². So s(1 + h) − s(1) = 32h − 16h². Average velocity = [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h = (32h − 16h²)/h = 32 − 16h feet per second, for h ≠ 0.

(b) An average velocity divides the change in height by the change in time. Over an interval of length zero the change in time is 0, so the quotient [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h would be 0/0, which is undefined. The average velocity formula therefore cannot be evaluated at h = 0 directly.

(c) Over 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.1 (h = 0.1): 32 − 16(0.1) = 30.4 ft/s. Check: s(1.1) = 70.4 − 19.36 = 51.04, and (51.04 − 48)/0.1 = 30.4. Over 0.9 ≤ t ≤ 1 (h = −0.1): 32 − 16(−0.1) = 33.6 ft/s. Check: s(0.9) = 57.6 − 12.96 = 44.64, and (48 − 44.64)/0.1 = 33.6.

(d) Instantaneous velocity at t = 1 = lim h→0 [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h = lim h→0 (32 − 16h) = 32 feet per second. The average velocities over intervals on either side of t = 1 (30.4 just after, 33.6 just before) lie on either side of 32, and as the interval length shrinks toward 0 the average velocities get closer and closer to 32. The instantaneous velocity is the limit of these average velocities.
item.verification_python:
import sympy as sp
t,h=sp.symbols('t h')
s=64*t-16*t**2
assert s.subs(t,1)==48
d=sp.expand(s.subs(t,1+h)-s.subs(t,1))
assert sp.simplify(d-(32*h-16*h**2))==0
q=sp.simplify(d/h)
assert sp.simplify(q-(32-16*h))==0
R=sp.Rational
assert s.subs(t,R(11,10))==R(5104,100)
assert (s.subs(t,R(11,10))-48)/R(1,10)==R(304,10)
assert s.subs(t,R(9,10))==R(4464,100)
assert (48-s.subs(t,R(9,10)))/R(1,10)==R(336,10)
assert q.subs(h,R(1,10))==R(304,10)
assert q.subs(h,R(-1,10))==R(336,10)
assert sp.limit(d/h,h,0)==32
assert R(304,10)<32<R(336,10)
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

parts.prompt: Find s(1 + h) − s(1) in simplified form. Then find a simplified expression in h for the average velocity of the ball over the time interval between t = 1 and t = 1 + h, where h ≠ 0.

criteria.text: Change in height: s(1 + h) − s(1) = 32h − 16h².
criteria.evidence: Shows s(1) = 48 and expands s(1 + h) = 48 + 32h − 16h², or otherwise arrives at 32h − 16h² with supporting algebra.
criteria.fix: Substitute 1 + h for every t, expand (1 + h)² carefully, then subtract s(1) = 48.

criteria.text: Average velocity: [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h = 32 − 16h feet per second, for h ≠ 0.
criteria.evidence: Divides the change in height by the change in time h and simplifies to 32 − 16h.
criteria.fix: Divide the change in height by the change in time h, then cancel the common factor h.

parts.prompt: Explain why the instantaneous velocity at t = 1 cannot be found by using the average velocity formula with an interval of length zero.

criteria.text: With h = 0 the change in time is zero, so the quotient [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h becomes 0/0 and the average velocity is undefined.
criteria.evidence: States that the change in the independent variable (time) would be zero, making the average rate of change a division by zero, so it is undefined.
criteria.fix: Note that average velocity divides by the change in time; say explicitly that a zero change in time makes the quotient undefined.

parts.prompt: Find the average velocity of the ball over the interval 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.1 and over the interval 0.9 ≤ t ≤ 1.

criteria.text: Average velocity over 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.1 is 30.4 feet per second.
criteria.fix: Substitute h = 0.1 into your part (a) expression or compute (s(1.1) − s(1))/0.1 directly.

criteria.text: Average velocity over 0.9 ≤ t ≤ 1 is 33.6 feet per second.
criteria.fix: For the interval ending at t = 1, use h = −0.1, or divide s(1) − s(0.9) by 0.1.

parts.prompt: Use a limit of average velocities to find the instantaneous velocity of the ball at t = 1, including units. Explain how your answer relates to the average velocities found in part (c).

criteria.text: Sets up the instantaneous velocity as the limit lim h→0 [s(1 + h) − s(1)]/h = lim h→0 (32 − 16h).
criteria.evidence: Writes a limit as h→0 of the average velocity expression (difference quotient or 32 − 16h), not a substitution of h = 0 into the unsimplified quotient.
criteria.fix: Write lim h→0 in front of the average velocity expression before evaluating; the limit is what defines instantaneous velocity.

criteria.text: Instantaneous velocity at t = 1 is 32 feet per second.
criteria.evidence: Evaluates the limit to 32 and includes units of feet per second.
criteria.fix: After simplifying to 32 − 16h, let h approach 0 and attach units of feet per second.

criteria.text: Explains that average velocities over intervals containing or ending at t = 1 approach 32 as the interval length shrinks, from both sides (30.4 below, 33.6 above).
criteria.evidence: States that as h→0 from either side the average velocities approach 32, noting 32 lies between the averages 30.4 and 33.6 or that they get closer to 32 as intervals shrink.
criteria.fix: Compare your part (c) averages to the limit and state that both approach it as the interval length shrinks toward zero.

item.title: Average Velocities Approaching an Instantaneous Velocity
item.stimulus: A cart moves along a straight track. Its position, in meters, at time t seconds is s(t) = 4t² + 2t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.
item.model_answer:
(a) s(1) = 4(1)² + 2(1) = 6 and s(1.5) = 4(2.25) + 3 = 12. Average velocity on [1, 1.5] = (12 − 6)/(1.5 − 1) = 6/0.5 = 12 meters per second.
s(1.1) = 4(1.21) + 2.2 = 7.04. Average velocity on [1, 1.1] = (7.04 − 6)/(1.1 − 1) = 1.04/0.1 = 10.4 meters per second.

(b) s(1 + h) = 4(1 + 2h + h²) + 2 + 2h = 6 + 10h + 4h². So s(1 + h) − s(1) = 10h + 4h², and for h ≠ 0, A(h) = (10h + 4h²)/h = 10 + 4h.
The quotient (s(1 + h) − s(1))/h cannot be evaluated at h = 0 because h is the change in time. When h = 0 the change in time is zero, so the quotient becomes 0/0, which involves division by zero. An average rate of change is undefined when the change in the independent variable is zero.

(c) Instantaneous velocity at t = 1 = lim h→0 (s(1 + h) − s(1))/h = lim h→0 (10 + 4h) = 10 meters per second.
In part (a), the average velocity was 12 m/s over an interval of length 0.5 and 10.4 m/s over an interval of length 0.1. As the interval starting at t = 1 shrinks, these average velocities get closer and closer to 10 m/s, and the limit of these average velocities is the instantaneous velocity at t = 1.
item.verification_python:
import sympy as sp
from fractions import Fraction as F
t,h=sp.symbols('t h')
s=4*t**2+2*t
assert s.subs(t,1)==6
assert s.subs(t,sp.Rational(3,2))==12
assert s.subs(t,sp.Rational(11,10))==sp.Rational(704,100)
a1=(s.subs(t,sp.Rational(3,2))-s.subs(t,1))/sp.Rational(1,2)
assert a1==12
a2=(s.subs(t,sp.Rational(11,10))-s.subs(t,1))/sp.Rational(1,10)
assert a2==sp.Rational(104,10)
assert sp.expand(s.subs(t,1+h))==6+10*h+4*h**2
A=sp.simplify((s.subs(t,1+h)-s.subs(t,1))/h)
assert sp.simplify(A-(10+4*h))==0
L=sp.limit(A,h,0)
assert L==10
assert sp.diff(s,t).subs(t,1)==10
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

parts.prompt: Find the average velocity of the cart over the time interval 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.5 and over the time interval 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.1. Show the computations that lead to your answers, and include units.

criteria.text: Average velocity over 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.5 is 12 meters per second.
criteria.evidence: Shows (s(1.5) − s(1))/(1.5 − 1) = (12 − 6)/0.5 = 12, or equivalent work, giving 12.
criteria.fix: Evaluate s at both endpoints, subtract, then divide by the length of the time interval, 0.5 seconds.

criteria.text: Average velocity over 1 ≤ t ≤ 1.1 is 10.4 meters per second.
criteria.fix: Compute s(1.1) = 4(1.21) + 2.2 = 7.04 carefully, then divide the change 1.04 by 0.1.

parts.prompt: For h ≠ 0, the average velocity of the cart over the interval from t = 1 to t = 1 + h is A(h) = (s(1 + h) − s(1))/h. Write A(h) as a simplified expression in h. Then explain why the quotient (s(1 + h) − s(1))/h cannot be evaluated at h = 0.

criteria.text: A(h) = 10 + 4h for h ≠ 0.
criteria.evidence: Expands s(1 + h) = 4(1 + h)² + 2(1 + h) = 6 + 10h + 4h², subtracts s(1) = 6, and divides 10h + 4h² by h to get 10 + 4h.
criteria.fix: Expand 4(1 + h)² + 2(1 + h) fully, subtract s(1), factor h from the numerator, then cancel it.

criteria.text: Explains that at h = 0 the change in time is zero, so the quotient divides by zero (gives 0/0) and the average velocity is undefined.
criteria.evidence: States that h is the change in the independent variable t, and when h = 0 the denominator is zero, so the average rate of change is undefined.
criteria.fix: Remember an average rate divides the change in output by the change in input; a zero change in input makes it undefined.

parts.prompt: Use a limit of the average velocities from part (b) to find the instantaneous velocity of the cart at t = 1. Explain how your answer is related to the values found in part (a), and include units.

criteria.text: Sets up the instantaneous velocity as lim h→0 of the average velocity, lim h→0 (s(1 + h) − s(1))/h = lim h→0 (10 + 4h).
criteria.evidence: Writes a limit as h→0 of the average velocity quotient or of 10 + 4h (or of an expression consistent with an earlier part (b) result).
criteria.fix: Write the instantaneous rate as the limit, as h approaches 0, of the average rate over [1, 1 + h].

criteria.text: Instantaneous velocity at t = 1 is 10 meters per second, with the explanation that the average velocities (12, then 10.4) approach 10 as the interval shrinks toward t = 1.
criteria.evidence: Gives 10 m/s from evaluating the limit and states that average velocities over shorter intervals starting at t = 1 get closer to 10, consistent with 12 and 10.4.
criteria.fix: After evaluating the limit, connect it to part (a): say the average velocities approach this value as the interval length shrinks to 0.
